entities.summary:
Dawlat Berdi, also known as Devlet Berdi, was the Khan of the Golden Horde from 1419 to 1421 and again from 1428 until his death in 1432. He was the son of Jabbar Berdi and a descendant of Berke Khan. Dawlat Berdi played a significant role in the politics of the Golden Horde during the late 15th century, navigating the complex web of alliances and rivalries between the Khanate and other neighboring powers.

He was a key figure in the Golden Horde's relations with the Grand Duchy of Moscow, which was expanding its influence in the region at the time. Dawlat Berdi's reign was marked by several conflicts with the Grand Duchy, including a major battle in 1420. Despite these challenges, Dawlat Berdi managed to maintain the Golden Horde's power and influence in the region.

Dawlat Berdi's legacy extends beyond his own lifetime, as he played a role in shaping the political landscape of the region during the late 15th century. His descendants continued to hold power in the Golden Horde for several decades after his death, and he remains an important figure in the history of the Khanate.

In recent years, Dawlat Berdi has been the subject of several historical studies, which have shed new light on his life and reign. These studies have highlighted the complexities of the Golden Horde's politics during the late 15th century and have provided a more nuanced understanding of Dawlat Berdi's role in shaping the region's history.
